starlink_vendor_spec.summary: Starlink publishes typical residential/roam download in the 25-220 Mbps range, upload 5-20 Mbps, latency 25-60ms under clear sky. These are vendor-published figures, not independently verified by this test program.

3gpp_ntn_latency.summary: 3GPP TR 38.821 defines a LEO non-terrestrial-network one-way latency budget of roughly 30-35ms, consistent with the low steady-state latency this rig measures when the link is up.

itu_t_y1541_class0.summary: ITU-T Y.1541 Class 0 (real-time, jitter-sensitive traffic) targets delay <=100ms, jitter <=50ms, and packet loss <=0.001. This rig's measured ping-drop rates (23-35% at obstructed sites) are far outside this class.

imda_fibre_qos_benchmark.summary: IMDA has no published QoS standard specific to satellite/wireless broadband. Its actual 'Quality of Service Framework for Retail Fixed-Line Broadband (Fibre) Internet Access Services' requires network availability >=99.9%, local latency <=30ms and international latency <=300ms (both round-trip, 95th percentile during the 4 busiest hours/day) -- but this legally applies only to fixed-line fibre BASPs with >=10% market share, not to Starlink Mini. Used here purely as a directional reference: this rig's measured p95 latency (~34ms) is in the same range as the fibre local-latency bar, but measured probe success (88.2% overall, as low as ~63% during the worst obstructed sessions) falls far short of the 99.9% fibre availability bar -- not a compliance finding, since Starlink isn't regulated under this framework and the measurement methodology differs (continuous 3-second polling vs monthly 5-min test calls).

site_type_confound.summary: The 3 real test sites (HDB home, MBC office, Punggol Park) differ in both obstruction level and site type (building vs open park). A single placement per site cannot separate 'better siting technique reduces obstruction' from 'an open park simply has less obstruction than a building'. The next recommended data collection step is 2-3 placements within the same building.
